scientific_name: Allium sativum var. ophioscorodon 'Kettle River Giant'

planting.note: Plant large cloves 3 inches deep in October-November after several nights of cold weather so roots establish before hard freeze.

directions: Kettle River Giant is a Porcelain-type hardneck garlic originating from the Kettle River valley near the Washington-British Columbia border, prized for producing some of the largest bulbs of any hardneck strain, often exceeding 3 inches across with just 4-6 oversized cloves per head. Grow it in rich, well-drained soil with consistent moisture through bulb sizing, and mulch heavily over winter in colder zones since Porcelain types are somewhat less cold-hardy than Rocambole strains. The flavor is strong and full-bodied with a lingering heat, and the tall, sturdy scapes make excellent garlic scape pesto in early summer. Choose this variety when garden space is limited but you still want big, easy-to-peel cloves for the kitchen.

planting.note: Plant cloves 2-3 inches deep 4-6 weeks before hard freeze so roots establish before ground freezes solid.

directions: Leningrad is a Porcelain-type hardneck garlic sourced from the historic seed collections of St. Petersburg, Russia, valued by cold-climate growers for exceptional winter hardiness and vigorous growth even after harsh, deep-freeze winters. Bulbs form with 4-6 large, easy-to-peel white-wrapped cloves and a robust, sharp flavor that mellows nicely when roasted. Because Porcelain types need a strong cold vernalization period, Leningrad performs best in northern gardens with reliably cold winters and struggles in warm-winter regions. Select this cultivar for its proven reliability in USDA zones 3-5 where many other garlic strains falter.

common_name: New York White Garlic (Heirloom Porcelain Hardneck)
scientific_name: Allium sativum var. ophioscorodon 'New York White'

planting.note: Plant cloves 2 inches deep in mid-fall once soil has cooled, mulching after the first hard frost.

directions: New York White is a long-preserved heirloom Porcelain hardneck strain maintained in northeastern American seed-saver collections for generations, valued for dependable bulb formation in cold Northeast winters and clean, glossy white wrappers. Bulbs typically produce 4-6 large cloves with a hot, pungent raw bite that sweetens dramatically when roasted or slow-cooked. As a true Porcelain type it needs a sustained cold period to vernalize properly, so gardeners in mild-winter climates should choose a different type. Grow it for its regional heirloom story and its reliability as an old New York homestead strain that has outlasted many modern hybrids.

planting.note: Plant cloves 2 inches deep in fall in well-drained soil; softneck Silverskins tolerate slightly later fall planting than hardneck types.

directions: Idaho Silverskin is a softneck garlic strain adapted to the high desert growing conditions of southern Idaho, producing tightly wrapped, bright white bulbs with 12-18 small, densely packed cloves ideal for braiding. It stores exceptionally well, often keeping firm for 9-12 months past harvest, longer than most hardneck types. Because it lacks a hard central stalk, the flexible leaves make traditional garlic braids easy to weave for kitchen storage or gifting. Choose this variety for its outstanding shelf life and adaptability to warmer, drier growing regions where hardneck types underperform.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or set out transplants/sets 2-4 weeks before last frost once soil is workable.

directions: Red Baron is a compact, early-maturing intermediate-day storage onion with deep red-purple skin and firm, pink-tinged white flesh with a moderately pungent, well-balanced flavor. Its smaller bulb size and quick maturity make it a favorite for gardeners who want reliable red onions without a long growing season, and its skins hold color and firmness well in storage for several months. Grow in fertile, well-drained soil with consistent moisture, keeping beds weed-free since onions compete poorly with weeds during bulb sizing. Choose Red Baron where garden space or season length is limited but a dependable, good-keeping red onion is still wanted.

planting.note: Direct sow with fresh seed once soil is workable in spring, in deep, loose, stone-free soil for straight roots.

directions: Countess is a modern F1 hybrid parsnip bred for strong resistance to canker, the fungal disease that causes unsightly brown-black shoulder rot in many older open-pollinated varieties. It produces long, smooth, uniform roots with a sweet, refined flavor and a notably high percentage of usable roots even in less-than-ideal soil. Because it is an F1 hybrid, seed should be purchased fresh each season rather than saved, and parsnip seed in general loses viability quickly regardless of source. Choose Countess over heirloom types like Hollow Crown where canker has historically been a problem in the garden.
